neighbours.label: A short i-vowel piece ('id', 'in', 'is', 'il') completing a split foreign name (Ab|id|in, Rash|id, B|oud|in), vs single-token names and ordinary English words
fire: The opening goal was scored by Rashid in the tenth minute.
The report was written by Zainal Abidin and two colleagues.
Last week the minister met Ahmed Obeid in Cairo.
The bakery owned by Marc Boudin closed in March.
The striker Seidou joined the club on a free transfer.
The paper lists Farid Rashid as the corresponding author.
On Friday the poet Abidin read from his new collection.
Coach Obeid praised the defense after the match.

predictions: 'id'/'in'/'is' pieces in split names 0.35-0.85; single-token names and common words under 0.1.
short: i-vowel piece in a split foreign name
notes: Card: gate-closed regime (99%), peaks 'id' x4, 'in' x4, 'n' x4, 'i', 'ɪ' in split names (Moyse|is, Se|id|u, Beile|in, E|id, Zay|n). Probe: 'Seidu' 0.832, 'Beilein' 0.813, 'Moyseis' 0.718, IPA 'ɪ' 1.136, 'Eid' 0.376, 'Leicestershire' 'ic' 0.370, 'Zayn' 0.358; 'barked at the mailman' 0.023. Tokenizer checked: Rash|id, Ab|id|in, O|be|id, B|oud|in, Se|id|ou all carry the piece; near misses use single-token names (Jay, Grace, Hope) or splits without an i-piece (Mb|eki, D|rog|ba).
